title: Lamb Chops with Mint Sauce
subtitle: Pan-fried or grilled lamb cutlets with fresh mint sauce
excerpt: Lamb cutlets or chops, cooked over high heat until pink inside with a caramelised crust, served with a sharp fresh mint sauce made from garden mint and vinegar. The British Sunday lunch treatment for lamb at its simplest.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mint sauce with lamb is one of the oldest flavour pairings in British cooking, documented as far back as the seventeenth century. Mint was grown in Britain for its ability to counteract the strong, fatty flavour of older mutton, which was the standard lamb product before the modern preference for young, tender lamb. The pairing persisted even as lamb became milder, and mint sauce remains the traditional British accompaniment to roast leg and grilled chops. French cuisine uses wine-based sauces; the British tradition insists on mint.

recipeTools.notes: Or a griddle pan for char marks.

content.text: The mint sauce is better made 30 minutes ahead so the sugar dissolves and the vinegar mellows slightly. For the chops: a very hot pan, a little oil, and 3 to 4 minutes per side for pink. Lamb cutlets are thin and cook fast; pull them off the heat the moment they feel springy rather than soft. They continue cooking as they rest.

Make the mint sauce: combine the chopped mint, vinegar, sugar, water, and a pinch of salt. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Taste and adjust: it should be sharp, herby, and just slightly sweet. Leave for 30 minutes.
Pat the lamb chops dry. Season on both sides with salt and pepper. Heat a frying pan or griddle over high heat until very hot. Add the oil.

Cook the chops in a single layer for 3 to 4 minutes per side for pink (62 C internal). Hold each chop fat-side down for 1 minute at the end to render the fat. Rest for 5 minutes before serving with the mint sauce.
